caption: The drawing depicts a lace-making setup composed of a green, rectangular cushion or pillow serving as the base, with rounded edges and a textured appearance. Attached to the base is a cylindrical roller covered in green and tan material, securely fastened at both ends by brown brackets. Around the roller, there is a lace pattern or design template. Numerous white threads extend from the roller to a row of wooden bobbins, each shaped with a bulbous end, arranged in two curved rows on the base. The bobbins are mostly light brown, with lighter highlights suggesting a polished wood texture. The threads cross and interlace between the roller and the bobbins, illustrating the process of lace-making. A red-brown wooden handle arches over the roller, with two pale cords, possibly used for carrying or securing the device, looping from each end of the handle and attaching to the sides of the base. The composition is centered on a plain beige background. The artist’s signature and the date “1940” are written in light cursive on the bottom right of the base.
title: Hand Lace Loom
